html:
Kigeli IV Rwabugiri was king of Rwanda in the second half of the 19th century, the last great ruler of the kingdom before colonial rule.

He fought almost constant wars, pushing the kingdom's power west to Lake Kivu and raiding neighbours, and brought outlying regions under chiefs he appointed. He imposed forced labour on Hutu farmers and spread cattle clientship, which sharpened the line between Hutu and Tutsi.

He died in 1895 on campaign, just as the first German officers arrived. His death set off a succession struggle, and the Germans backed the winning faction. The state he left, centralised and divided, was the one that Belgium later ruled through, and that the revolution of 1959 overturned.
sum: Kigeli IV Rwabugiri was king of Rwanda in the second half of the 19th century, the last great ruler of the kingdom before colonial rule.
